newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish floods hit mainly grain crops - analyst.
newsitem.headline: Polish floods hit mainly grain crops - analyst.

text.p: Heavy flooding in southern and western Poland over the last weeks which covered some 400,000 hectares of arable land may have inundated as much as 140,000 ha of grain fields, a senior analyst said on Tuesday.

"Up to half of the estimated 400,000 hectars of inundated arable land is likely to be unused fields and pastures in and around river beds and about 70 percent of the rest could be grain fields," said Michal Kisiel, chief grain analyst at the government-funded Farm Economy and Food Management Institutue.
Kisiel said not enough information was available to make accurate estimates of crop losses caused by the flooding.
Kisiel reiterated earlier estimates which placed Poland's grain output in 1997 around the lower end of a forecast range between 23.6 and 24.7 million tonnes.
The Agriculture ministry on Tuesday said no new damage data was available, but updated information may flow in from various regions before the end of the week.
"We still don't have anything new," a ministry spokesman told Reuters over the telephone.

Last week Agriculture Minister Jaroslaw Kalinowski said 370,000 to 400,000 ha of arable land were flooded and the total cost of lost crops and recultivation in flooded regions may reach one billion zlotys.
